newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli minister visits Lebanon militia head.
newsitem.headline: Israeli minister visits Lebanon militia head.

text.p: Israel's defence minister on Tuesday visited the commander of its South Lebanon Army (SLA) to show support after Lebanon passed a death sentence in absentia on him for collaborating with the Jewish state.
Israel's Channel Two Television showed Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai embracing SLA militia commander General Antoine Lahd at his headquarters in Marjayoun south Lebanon.
Lahd, a 69-year-old former Lebanese army major-general, heads the 3,000-strong SLA that helps Israel occupy a strip of south Lebanon to ward off cross-frontier guerrilla raids on northern Israel.

"I am encouraging General Lahd. We will continue to support Lahd and his military forces and the citizens of this area. It is necessary for the freedom of Lebanon and it is necessary for the security of Israel," Mordechai said.
A Lebanese military court on Friday convicted Lahd of collaborating with Israel. Lebanon is officially at war with the Jewish state.
Israel said on Saturday the Lebanese sentence against Lahd was aimed at wrecking peace prospects.
